title: Control-Flow Complexity
definition: Control-flow complexity is the reasoning burden created by the number, interaction, and nesting of possible execution paths.
purpose: Make path coverage, review difficulty, and change risk visible before syntax becomes unmanageable.
history: Control-flow graphs and cyclomatic complexity formalized aspects of path structure; cognitive-complexity approaches later emphasized human understandability.
mental_model: Every decision is a fork on a map; nesting makes a fork depend on earlier forks and increases the context a reader must retain.
analogy: A road network with intersections; it fails as a complete model because program paths may be infeasible and state-dependent.
common_mistakes: Treating one metric as a universal quality verdict
Reducing indentation while preserving hidden coupling
industry_notes: Metrics are investigation signals, not substitutes for context, behavior, and review evidence.
ai_notes: Ask AI to enumerate assumptions and feasible paths instead of merely reporting a complexity number.
interview_notes: Ask why two visually similar functions can impose different reasoning burdens.
